Welcome to Beachborough Prep, near Brackley
We are an outstanding Nursery, Pre-Prep and Prep School for children aged 2.5 years to 13 years, based in the village of Westbury and close to Buckingham and Brackley where learning and having fun go hand-in-hand.
Nestled in 35 acres of land on the Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire and Northamptonshire borders, our children are happy and successful. We believe that is because we focus on creating and inspiring a nurturing learning adventure where each and every child can flourish achieving things, they simply didn’t think were possible and preparing them for life as ‘world ready’ citizens.

pageCache.text:
Reception
In Reception, children continue to follow the national Early Years curriculum, with the addition of learning French and Music with specialist teachers. They learn to write in cursive script, which is beneficial to their writing ability across the board. They learn in small groups with lots of individual attention from their teachers, and they enjoy a wide range of outdoor activities in the woods and garden, but especially in the outdoor area of their classroom which has a canopy which can even be used when it’s raining.
Each term, Reception classes set off on an exciting trip to a place that will help to bring the topic they are studying to life. Recent examples include The Heritage Motor Centre when they were exploring transport and the Natural History Museum in Oxford when the theme was dinosaurs. From the spring term, they can choose activities and clubs from the co-curricular programme.
With the national Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum as our framework for Nursery, Kindergarten and our Reception classes, we focus on teaching, supporting and challenging each child within the seven key areas of learning:
Personal, social and emotional development
Communication and language
Physical development
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the world
Expressive arts and design

Independent Schools Inspection Report
Beachborough Prep is regularly inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), with our latest inspection taking place in December 2025.
We are incredibly proud to share that Beachborough has been awarded a Significant Strength in our latest report, alongside meeting all inspection standards. A Significant Strength is a rare and prestigious recognition within the ISI framework, and we are thrilled to have received this accolade for the following area:
‘Leaders provide pupils with meaningful opportunities to contribute to the local and wider community, many of which involve pupil-led initiatives. Involvement in these initiatives aligns with the school’s values of empathy and engagement. Leaders’ active promotion of pupils’ involvement in the wider community has a highly beneficial impact on the pupils’ social development and empathy and is a significant strength of the school.’

Charity & Outreach
Charity work at Beachborough Prep is an integral part of life at Beachborough School and our community is committed to fundraising. We are top fundraisers and proud to support a variety of different charities, locally, nationally and internationally. Each year, we continue to think of creative ways to support local, national and international communities. We raise tens of thousands of pounds, annually, so that we can support different charities which help others in urgent need.
We believe that it is essential that our pupils grow up understanding how important it is to support others; we teach them to reach out to others in need. Charity work becomes part of their everyday lives. At Beachborough Prep we create good citizens who understand the importance of charity work, and have the lifelong skills and desire to help others in need.
Throughout the year, we organise many different events. The whole school is involved – from the tiniest tots in our Nursery to our teenagers in Form Vlll. We collect sponsorship, sell raffle tickets, bake cakes, dress-up, clean bedrooms, sing carols, sell seeds, wash cars, design hats, splash at pool parties, dance at discos, sell pre-loved items, donate food, abseil, eat porridge, take part in sports events, camp-out and even donate birthday money.
One of our most important and enduring charitable relationships is with the charity Mary’s Meals – an organisation founded on the simple, yet vital, principle of providing the poorest children in the world with a meal at school, every day. Over the last twelve years, the Beachborough community has raised over £90,000 for Mary’s Meals. We raise more money per pupil than any other school in the United Kingdom. Beachborough Prep has a relationship with NThola Primary School in northern Malawi, who we support by raising enough funds to pay for every child on the school roll, to receive one mug of vitamin enriched porridge, daily, for a whole year. Sponsoring a school is an amazing gift. We are giving some of the poorest children in the world, hope for a brighter future.
Our fundraising at Beachborough Prep is extraordinary due to the good will of our pupils, parents, staff and former Beachborough alumni who continue to respond generously to each and every fundraising event. Raising money at Beachborough unleashes our children’s creativity and encourages them to be enterprising as well as helping them to become kind, responsible citizens. The charity work that we do, demands that we use all six of the CREATE skills: Communication, Reflection, Empathy, Adaptability, Tenacity, and Engagement. It broadens our minds and makes us part of the wider world.
Here at Beachborough Prep, we are committed to making a difference and changing lives for the better for those that need our help – but most of all – our charity work is great fun!
“Conemur Tenues Grandia” – Though we are small, let us try for great things.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care | Private School Brackley | Beachborough School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
We recognise families have different needs, and that everybody’s daily routines can be different. We have morning and after-school care to make your day a bit less stressful, knowing that your child is cared for in their school environment with familiar staff.
In Nursery to pre-prep 2, Wraparound Care at Beachborough Prep is available from 8am in the morning until lessons begin, and then again after lessons end in the afternoon until 6pm. During these times children play in the main foyers of The Boardman, a variety of toys are on offer as well as lots of activities like drawing and Lego.
The atmosphere is relaxed and calm, and the regular Boardman staff are there to supervise and look after the children. It is important that they are in a cosy, caring environment with teachers they know well, especially towards the end of the day when they can be tired.
New for September 2025, Breakfast Club is offered from 07.30am-8.00am for children in Forms III-VIII. Please note there is an additional fee for attending Breakfast Club.
At 4.30 everyone goes up to the dining room for tea. If it is warm enough, the children then go and play outside in the playground or the climbing frame and trim trail on the front lawn.
In Forms lll and lV children can stay in aftercare until 6:45pm. Once their school day finishes at 4:30pm, they enjoy a hot meal in the Dining Hall and are then supervised in the Boardman by a member of staff and gap students until you wish to collect them.
Formal lessons in Forms V – Vlll finish at 5.05pm. Aftercare changes from the supervised play offered in Form IV and children are now offered the option of supervised homework on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday each week and an extensive choice of activities from the co-curricular programme on Monday and Thursday evenings until 6.45pm.
The majority of pupils opt to do their homework in school under teacher supervision, with a break for an evening meal from 5.00pm to 5.30pm, so at the end of the day all their work is completed and they can go home to relax.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery & Reception | Pre-Prep School | Beachborough School
pageCache.text:
Nursery, Kindergarten & Reception
In Nursery, Kindergarten and Reception, we focus on learning through play, developing relationships and acquiring social skills. Our Early Years staff are highly qualified, well experienced, caring individuals who are passionate about inspiring children to love learning.
Our below Early Years Showcase Film will provide you with an insight into the Early Years at Beachborough Prep.

Kindergarten
Kindergarten (Pre-School) is a gentle and joyful beginning to a child’s educational journey. At this stage, the children are gently introduced to the routines they will encounter in the more structured environment of Reception so that they are well-prepared when the time comes to move up. The Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum is taught through play, with the focus on enjoyment and fun.
Our approach is rooted in the magic of play not just as an activity, but as the foundation of all meaningful learning in the Early Years. Through carefully planned and thoughtfully resourced experiences, children explore the world around them, develop confidence, and build key skills across all areas of learning.
Phonics and early mathematical thinking are naturally woven into our daily provision, helping children to develop their early literacy and numeracy in a way that feels engaging and exciting. Alongside this, we nurture creativity, curiosity, communication and physical development, supporting each child on their unique developmental journey.
We organise each term’s learning around a different topic, linking a wide range of activities and providing a thematic focus. Using inspirational, interesting resources and a wide range of activities, we nurture our children so that they reach their full potential and their Early Learning Goals in time for moving up to Reception with sparked imagination, ready to explore hands-on experiences that promote inquiry, problem-solving and joyful discovery.
The children in Kindergarten also benefit from their weekly specialist Music and PE sessions which help to support their physical coordination, self-expression, and overall wellbeing. We even begin teaching them a little French, because the younger they start learning a foreign language, the better! We work in close partnership with parents in carefully documenting the children’s progress and in celebrating their achievements. We use an interactive online journal, Tapestry, to capture and communicate each child’s individual learning journey, helping to build a strong bridge between home and school.
Above all, Kindergarten is a place where children feel safe, loved, and valued – a space where they can thrive, explore, and begin their lifelong love of learning.
Our Beachborough Explorers Stay & Play events are the perfect opportunity for pre-school aged children and their parents to explore the Beachborough Prep learning environment. Head to our events pages to find out more.

Nursery
Nursery is where many children take their very first steps into education and at Beachborough Prep, we ensure that those steps are filled with warmth, care, and a deep sense of belonging.
Our nurturing environment is designed to help each child feel safe, valued, and understood from the moment they join us. We believe that the Early Years are about building strong, emotional foundations and our focus in Nursery is on helping the children settle happily into life at Beachborough, developing trusting relationships, learning routines, and building confidence and independence in a patient and gentle way. Each child is celebrated as an individual and we foster a culture of kindness, acceptance and purposeful play.
Learning at this age is rooted in explorative play and discovery and children are introduced to a wide variety of sensory, creative and imaginative experiences that support their development across all areas of learning, gently building on skills which will help them as they grow, such as listening, sharing, speaking, and moving, with confidence.
Our Nursery and Kindergarten children share an inviting, well-equipped indoor space as well an an outdoor garden that encourages connection with nature and with one another. Sometimes everyone is all together playing, at other times we split into Nursery and Kindergarten groups, so we can enjoy different activities. Children can join us from 2½ onwards, moving through to Kindergarten the year they turn 4. The children are free to explore, create and play each day outside and within our dedicated Forest School, where they can learn to love and care for the natural world around them.

pageCache.text:
School History
One of the oldest prep schools in the country, Beachborough was originally founded in Surrey in 1910, by an energetic young teacher called Frederick Edmondson Chappell.
The school was initially called the Downs, named after the rolling hills it nestled in, but after several moves and having miraculously survived the First World War without its founder and headmaster (who was busy on the front line), it settled at Beachborough Park near Folkestone in Kent. From the top of Summerhouse Hill, within the grounds, the coast of France was clearly visible and it was this summerhouse that gave the school its badge.
“Conemur tenues grandia – Although we are small, let us try for great things.”
The name stuck, even after the school moved again when World War Two broke out and the MOD requisitioned the building. From here, it began its gradual journey westwards, first to Stockbridge in Hampshire where it merged with another prep school, and then finally to Northamptonshire where Fred Chappell, scouring the countryside on his motorbike, had found a new home. Here, in this idyllic location on the edge of a pretty village, the boys of Westbury Manor School suddenly found themselves with a new headmaster, new fellow pupils and a new name – Beachborough Prep had arrived.
Fred couldn’t have done a better job in finding himself, his wife and his school a new home. When Fred Chappell retired in 1958 he formed the school into an Educational Trust with a Board of Governors. The first Headmaster to run the school as a Trust was Eric Sprawson (1958 to 1974). Since then the Headmasters have been Andrew Jackson (1975 -1979), Simon Carder (1979 – 1988), Tony Boardman (1988 – 2005), Jonathan Whybrow (2005 -2013), Jeremy Banks (2013 – 2018), Christian Pritchard (2018- 2023) and Simone Mitchell (2023- date). If Fred came back today he would doubtless be surprised and impressed by the new buildings and facilities, but reassured by how beautiful and familiar so much else is.
The lovely 17th century Manor House is the heart of the school, especially in the winter when the fire in the main hall is lit. While it is beautiful and historic on the outside, the interior is firmly in the 21st century with ICT Suites, an Art Studio, Dining Room, a Library, Music Rooms, Language Suites, a Food Technology Kitchen, Science Labs and airy modern Classrooms. The terrace beside the Manor House leads down to a sweeping lawn with a playground at the bottom, there is a bridge over the stream leading to expansive playing fields, while on the other side of the car park there are tennis courts, the forest school, the woods and a path that takes you to the wetland’s areas. Elsewhere on the school site, there has been an ambitious building programme in recent years. In 2005, The Boardman was built to house the Nursery to Form IV, and we celebrated the school’s centenary in 2010 with a brand-new sports hall complete with a 5 a side football pitch, badminton courts, a trampoline, cricket and archery nets. These facilities compliment the outdoor Astroturf, tennis and netball courts and of course, the acres of grass playing fields. The old gym has been re-developed into a theatre where plays and music are performed regularly as well as larger-scale events, concerts, assemblies, and other occasions when the whole school gets together, take place in here. The theatre is fully equipped with lighting and sound technology that gives performances at Beachborough a truly professional feel and pupils the opportunity to learn to use this kind of equipment.
In 2017, the TED (technology, engineering and design) suite was opened where children can learn to use the very latest technology. In this state-of-the-art facility, they will learn coding, robotics, digital design, 3-D printing and laser cutting – skills they will need in our increasingly technological world.
Classrooms at Beachborough are well-resourced with the latest technology, smartboards, and a wealth of electronic learning devices. We have specialist laboratory classrooms for science and a library where children can enjoy reading a wide range of books.
All of these facilities provide a superb setting for the excellent, wide-ranging education that children at Beachborough Prep benefit from.

pageCache.text:
Open Days
We are pleased that you are considering a Beachborough Prep adventure for your child. To enable you to gain a real sense of our school community, we warmly invite you to come and visit.
How can I book a visit or tour of the school?
Every day is an open day at Beachborough Prep! If you would like to arrange your individual tour, our Admissions Team will be delighted to find a suitable date for you to visit. A typical visit will include a full tour of the school and an informal conversation with our Head Mrs Mitchell. Following an individual tour, all prospective pupils are invited to register with us and to come along and experience a day at school in the form of a Taster Day or a Discovery Session for our younger learners.
What will I see during a school visit?
At Beachborough Prep, we believe that seeing the school in action is the best way to understand what makes our community so special. During your visit, you will experience the energy of our classrooms, the enthusiasm of our pupils, and the dedication of our staff. Our aim is to give you a genuine insight into daily life at the school, so that you can feel confident that Beachborough is the right fit for your child and your family.
What facilities can I explore during my visit?
Your tour will provide the opportunity to explore our extensive grounds and facilities, from academic classrooms to outdoor learning spaces. You will also have the chance to observe lessons, meet pupils, and gain a sense of the supportive and nurturing environment that defines Beachborough. Our Admissions Team is committed to making the process as smooth and informative as possible. They are available to answer any questions you may have about entry points, assessments, and availability. For more information, please visit our Admissions page.
What are taster days and discovery sessions?
Taster Days and Discovery Sessions are designed to help children feel confident and excited about joining Beachborough Prep. These experiences allow prospective pupils to take part in lessons, meet new friends, and engage in a variety of activities, offering a true taste of school life. Following a successful Taster Day or Discovery Session, a formal offer will be made by our Admissions Team.
How do I start the admissions journey at Beachborough Prep?
We understand that choosing the right school is an important decision for any family. Whether you begin with a visit or explore further through our Curriculum and Co-Curricular pages, we look forward to welcoming you and helping you discover all that Beachborough has to offer. Please do get in touch with our Admissions Team, who will be happy to help you take the first step.
